title: Grouping and Counting 🧮
ques: Write a query to count the number of users in each `country`. Use `GROUP BY`.
explanation: `GROUP BY` aggregates rows with the same values, and `COUNT(*)` calculates the number of rows in each group.

title: Filtering Aggregations 🎯
ques: Write a query to find countries with more than 100 users. Use `GROUP BY` and `HAVING`.

answer.content:
SELECT country, COUNT(*) as user_count
FROM users
GROUP BY country
HAVING COUNT(*) > 100;

explanation: The `HAVING` clause is used instead of `WHERE` to filter groups after an aggregation is applied.

title: Creating Indexes ⚡
ques: Write an SQL command to create an index named `idx_email` on the `email` column of the `users` table to speed up searches.
explanation: Indexes significantly improve data retrieval speeds for columns frequently used in `WHERE` clauses.
